headline: The Guru Tegh Bahadur date passed yesterday without its Short; the Goa shikha Short went up instead. Publish it by 26 November for search or press Drop. The Indonesia long-form is still adding subscribers every day, so its Bali follow-up is this week's main job, with the Churchill Short for 30 November.

top3.topic: Guru Tegh Bahadur, a day late
top3.signal: His date was 24 November and no Short went up. His name is no longer trending on X; the searched phrase “guru tegh bahadur history” stays all year.
top3.recommendation: Publish by the evening of 26 November or press Drop. Title starts with his name, Aurangzeb's order in sentence one, an act of state and not a martyr story.

top3.signal: Five days out; recording is due this week. His English Wikipedia readership is at its usual level. A British minister compared Zelensky to him this week, so the praise is in the news.
top3.recommendation: Record by 28 November and publish the morning of 30 November, his name first in the title. One document, its date, then what was decided.

top3.signal: Nine days out, and a Short is already written and sourced, not recorded: “The Year Britain Banned Sati, Englishmen Were Selling Their Wives”. Under the channel's last sati Short, a liked comment made the same point: “People who burned witches in Europe stopped Sati in India”.
top3.recommendation: Record by 2 December and publish the morning of 4 December. Before recording, settle the line the script itself flags: “never wrote a law” needs a source or softer wording.

more.signal: The second Ayodhya Short is written and waiting for the owner's edit: the slab that came out of the rubble on 6 December 1992, and the museum stone it was said to be. The first, “Irfan Habib’s Controversy: What the Court Record Actually Says #ThePrintIndia”, held viewers better than the channel's usual Short, 75.7% average view.
more.recommendation: Edit it this week and publish the morning of 6 December, with pinned comments linking the two Shorts to each other. Keep it to the two stones and the dates.

skipped.signal: Still earning: the box-office news has it entering India's top four. The channel's last film Short (15 November) has 1,769 views.
skipped.recommendation: Skip new film Shorts. The Malay Ravana Short already written is the last one, because it sends viewers to the Indonesia long-form.

skipped.signal: The 2008 Mumbai attacks are on the calendar for 26 November, beside Constitution Day. Nothing is written.
skipped.recommendation: Skip. A recap of news the audience already lived through gave the feed nothing to push here before (the Operation Sindoor video), and one day is not enough to find the angle nobody else has.

whats_working: “How the Ramayana Was REWRITTEN to Convert Hindus” carried long-form: long-form views rose 91.1% week over week, and new long-forms have brought 658 subscribers this month against 104 planned. Over 28 days long-form earns 85.4% of the net subscribers videos bring.

The video that brings the most subscribers per view in the 90-day window is “How One Man Who Never Visited India Wrote Its History”, at 12.3 net per 1,000 views. Its lesson: “Name the villain, convict him with a document or payment he cannot deny, then end on who is still repeating him today.” The Churchill Short and the Bali video are both built on it.
whats_wrong: Long-form brings fewer subscribers per view than it used to: 7.3 per 1,000 over the 365-day window, now below its usual range. The three Ramayana long-forms bring 3.9, 2 and 1.1 per 1,000; only 41.7% of November's long-form views were engaged views, and the 7-day average view is 27.9%. Probable cause: most plays come from the Home feed and are not real viewing, and the stories with no culprit do not get followed. Test: the Bali video names a culprit and a date; compare its subscribers per 1,000 on day three with the Indonesia one's.

Shorts views fell 83.2% week over week: 23,123 in the 7 days to 2026-11-22 against 137,582 the week before. Correction: yesterday's brief put this down to the Ramayana film losing screens; today's box-office news has it still earning on day 20 and entering India's top four. What stopped is the channel's own film Shorts: “Every Ramayana Kept One Rule. The Ramayana Movie BROKE It” (15 November) has 1,769 views against 79,092 for the one of 11 November. Probable cause: eight Ramayana Shorts between 30 October and 15 November, and the feed stops trying more of the same. Test: the Malay Ravana Short is the last one; if its first day is slower than the Goa shikha Short's 46.9 views an hour, no more film Shorts.

Dated Shorts the brief asks for are not getting made: Tegh Bahadur missed its date and Tipu lapsed on 24 November, while the two Shorts that went up since 22 November, British officers' pay and the Goa shikha tax, were scripts already written. Probable cause: the brief kept picking dates with nothing on disk. Test: the next two dates, Sati on 4 December and Babri on 6 December, already have written scripts; see whether they ship.

actions.action: Upload the Malay Ravana Short today or tomorrow: title starting “Ravana”, Related video set to the Indonesia long-form, its link in the pinned comment, and the text named on screen as the Malay “Hikayat Seri Rama”.
actions.rationale: It is written (19 November, from the owner's draft) and was built to send viewers to the Indonesia long-form while that video still draws them. Viewers there have already said this version is Malay. Whether a Short sends viewers on is a guess.

actions.action: Test a new title and the designer's thumbnail on “The Church That Ran Britain's PRISON Camps” in Studio's Test & Compare.
actions.rationale: Over the 365-day window it brings 34.3 subscribers per 1,000 views, the best on the channel, on only 1,079 views: the people who find it subscribe, and too few find it. That the title is the reason is a guess.

actions.action: Check in Studio why “How Jati's evolve organically ?” still has 21 views since 3 November.
actions.rationale: A public Short gets at least a few views a day; this points to a visibility setting or a restriction, not the topic.

actions.action: Set GA4_PROPERTY_ID in .env so the brief can read itiha.info's traffic.
actions.rationale: Search Console alone is thin: every query that shows is the brand name.

growth.verdict: Needs 224 net subscribers a day. The channel does 65.04/day, so the target is a **3.4x** change in rate. Every lever this channel has demonstrated, pulled at once (scenario "1. Current rate, nothing changes"), reaches 65/day — still 3.4x short. At that ceiling rate 100,000 arrives on 2030-05-05, 3.4 years out.

scenarios.name: 1. Current rate, nothing changes
assumptions: Measured: channel_totals_daily, everything the channel publishes, last 28 days.
Same formats, same cadence, same lane mix.
Includes the channel's one breakout: "Chakla: How the British Raj Created a ‘Licensed Vice’ System" is 1282 of the 3,241 subscribers that 22 fresh long-form videos produced.

scenarios.name: 2. Stop Shorts, same effort into long-form (no breakout)
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 30/day (839 of 1,691 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Measured: 22 long-form and 105 Shorts published in the last 365 days.
ASSUMPTION (not measured): 6 Shorts cost what 1 long-form costs, so the Shorts become 17.5 more long-form videos a year — 39.5 in total.
Measured: MEDIAN 33 subscribers per fresh long-form video. The mean is 147, inflated by one breakout, so the median is the honest number for planned output.
Gives up the 450 subscribers a year the Shorts brought in; they are simply absent from this total.
Below scenario 1 because scenario 1 contains a breakout and this one does not. That is the point, not an error.

scenarios.name: 3. All long-form, all revision lane (no breakout)
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 30/day (839 of 1,691 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Scenario 2's cadence, every topic chosen from the revision lane.
Measured on the same fresh set: 9 revision long-form videos, median 69 subscribers, against 33 for fresh long-form overall.
ASSUMPTION: the lane median holds as output scales. It rests on a small number of videos and is the weakest link here.

scenarios.name: 4. Scenario 3 plus one breakout a quarter
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 30/day (839 of 1,691 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Scenario 3, plus four videos a year performing like the best video the channel has ever published.
Measured: "Chakla: How the British Raj Created a ‘Licensed Vice’ System" brought 1,282 subscribers on 73,126 views.
ASSUMPTION: a breakout that size can be produced to order, four times a year. The channel has produced one.
